# Fixed-effective-capacity makes keep ordinary escape behavior at every
# opt tier: non-escaping fixed makes never heap-allocate, escaping ones do.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd m
go test -count=1 -O=0 .
go test -count=1 -O=1 .
go test -count=1 -O=2 .
go test -count=1 -O=3 .
logos test -count=1 -O=1 .
logos test -count=1 -O=2 .
logos test -count=1 -O=3 .

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/fixedmakeparity

go 1.27

-- m/fixed.go --
package fixedmakeparity

var escaped []byte
var sink byte

//go:noinline
func recFixed(n int) byte {
	if n <= 0 {
		return 0
	}
	b := make([]byte, 200)
	b[0] = byte(n)
	b[199] = byte(n >> 1)
	return recFixed(n-1) + b[0] + b[199]
}

//go:noinline
func fixedSmall() byte {
	b := make([]byte, 16)
	b[0] = 3
	return b[15] + b[0]
}

//go:noinline
func fixedEscape() {
	escaped = make([]byte, 0, 16)
}

-- m/fixed_test.go --
package fixedmakeparity

import "testing"

func TestFixedMakeTierParity(t *testing.T) {
	if got := testing.AllocsPerRun(20, func() { sink = recFixed(5) }); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("recursive fixed make took %v allocations, want none", got)
	}
	if got := testing.AllocsPerRun(20, func() { sink = fixedSmall() }); got != 0 {
		t.Errorf("small fixed make took %v allocations, want none", got)
	}
	if got := testing.AllocsPerRun(20, func() { fixedEscape() }); got < 1 {
		t.Errorf("escaping fixed make took %v allocations, want the heap", got)
	}
}
